notes: 17 cases: 11 positive (should_trigger true) / 6 negative (should_trigger false). By origin: 7 golden (authored), 4 real-trace (byte-verbatim production user turns), 6 negative (authored single-axis near-misses). PROVENANCE: the four real-trace prompts were lifted from the raw CLI transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-broomva-broomva/, each from the last genuine user turn preceding a Skill{"skill":"handoff"} tool_use in the same file (isSidechain false, type user); the exact file, timestamp and grep method are in verification_log.real_trace_verbatim. REGISTER: authored prompts are written in the same voice as those production turns (lowercase, comma splices, dropped apostrophes, no em dashes). Measured, not assumed: not one of the 31 production handoff turns contains an em dash or an en dash, and neither does any prompt here, so a polished em-dash prompt would be out of distribution and would measure routing on a text style the skill never sees. TRIGGER-SURFACE SPLIT (the central design decision, and the honest part): of the 31 user turns that immediately precede a production invocation, 30 name the skill literally, usually as /handoff; the 31st (f185e467-...) is an image-attachment turn whose only text is the CLI's own caption '[Image: original 4180x4472, displayed at 1869x2000. ...]', i.e. no user prose at all, so ZERO production invocations were routed by paraphrase. Method, re-run 2026-07-28: for each of the 31 Skill{handoff} tool_use events, walk back to the nearest type=user, isSidechain=false event that carries typed text - skipping tool_result echoes and harness injections, which is what an earlier walk-back failed to skip. A scan of every user turn in all 1063 UUID transcripts for the description's paraphrase triggers (where we are / left off / resume tomorrow / for the next session / for the next agent / pickup) with the word 'handoff' excluded returned 117 raw hits collapsing to 29 unique turns, and NONE of them asks for a handoff: 28 are harness-injected text (compaction summaries, 'Base directory for this skill:' preambles, task-notification blocks, platform base prompts) and exactly ONE is a turn a human typed - 'Continue from where you left off.', which is a resume instruction, not a request for a doc. RE-MEASURED 2026-07-28: the 117 figure reproduces exactly; the previously recorded '7 unique turns, two injected / one compaction / four status questions' did NOT reproduce and has been replaced by the counts above. So the paraphrase-inference load is carried entirely by the 7 authored goldens, none of which contains the string 'handoff'; the 4 real-trace cases measure the dominant production shape, and each of them will raise the runner's 'prompt contains the literal skill name' warning. That warning is accepted deliberately for production evidence, not overlooked. CLEAN-WORKSPACE DISCIPLINE: every case runs in a fresh temp dir holding only .claude/skills/handoff, with no git repo, no branch, no open PRs, no docs/ and no knowledge graph. Every positive therefore carries the session state it wants written up INLINE in the prompt; no case names a filesystem path or depends on repo state. See each case's workspace_requires.

execution_contract.advisory: Documentation only - runner.py does not read this object; it is here so the intended contract is reviewable and so drift between intent and CLI flags is visible. Values mirror runner.py's module constants at authoring time.
execution_contract.workspace: clean temp dir per trial; skill installed at .claude/skills/handoff; --setting-sources project; --permission-mode bypassPermissions; --no-session-persistence
execution_contract.negative_semantics: CORRECTED 2026-07-28 - the prior wording said a triggered negative fails 'BEFORE expected_checks are consulted', which misreads the runner. Actually observed at runner.py:1026: run_checks(case.expected_checks, ctx) is called FIRST, on every path, and its results are attached to the TrialResult; the should_trigger branch is only entered afterwards (runner.py:1030-1051). What is true is PRECEDENCE, not ordering: at runner.py:1047 a should_trigger:false trial whose transcript.triggered(skill) is true returns FAIL('over-triggered on a near-miss prompt') regardless of whether its checks passed. So the checks on a negative are additive assertions about what the run did INSTEAD of firing - recorded either way, never able to rescue an over-trigger.
execution_contract.positive_semantics: Same correction. A positive that did not trigger returns FAIL('skill did not trigger') at runner.py:1038 - or RECOVERED at runner.py:1032-1037 if transcript.read_skill_content found the run answering by reading SKILL.md off disk - with its check results recorded but not consulted for the verdict. expected_checks on a positive therefore grade the OUTCOME of a run that did fire: for this skill that outcome is a durable file, which is why documents_finding is on all 11 positives (re-counted 2026-07-28: 11/11).

known_gaps.no_paraphrase_sourced_real_trace: There is no real-trace case in which the user requests a handoff WITHOUT naming it. That is not an oversight and not a shortage of searching: the scan described in notes covered every user turn in all 1063 transcripts (re-counted 2026-07-28; the corpus grows, so this number is a timestamp, not a constant) and found zero such turns. The description advertises triggers on 'where we are', 'leave off', 'for the next session', 'resume tomorrow' and 'pickup', and this workspace has never used any of them to ask for one. The 7 goldens are therefore testing an advertised trigger surface that production has never exercised, which is exactly the surface most likely to be broken and least likely to be noticed.
known_gaps.excluded_real_trace_minimal_turn: The production turn 'sorry no, we need to handoff' (~/.claude/projects/-Users-broomva-conductor-workspaces-sri-monterrey/003ec38d-d5ae-4b4c-a9af-b4e001df8f4c.jsonl) was deliberately NOT shipped, and so were 'lets /handoff' and 'good, please /handoff'. CLAIM CORRECTED 2026-07-28: this said 'in production each arrived after 2000+ events of arc context', which does not hold. Measured by counting the events preceding each occurrence in its own transcript: 'sorry no, we need to handoff' arrived 2405 events in (n=1); 'lets /handoff' has 10 occurrences spanning 161 to 5264 preceding events (median 1343); 'good, please /handoff' has 3 spanning 207 to 2517 (median 1685). So the true statement is that they arrive at widely varying depths, typically well into a session but sometimes early. The exclusion stands on the argument, not the number: each of these turns carries no state of its own, so it is only interpretable against whatever arc preceded it. Stripped of that in a clean temp dir there is no session to compress, so asking the user what to hand off is arguably the CORRECT response - and the case would score it FAIL. A case that punishes correct behaviour is a false-fail generator, so the floor-case trigger test is left uncovered rather than faked.
known_gaps.excluded_real_trace_env_dependent: 'lets pull and make sure git status is clean, then /handoff' and 'please /handoff #3 so that we can work on it on the proper workspace' are both real and both excluded: the first needs a git remote, the second an antecedent list item. Each would fail for environmental reasons unrelated to whether the description routes.
known_gaps.documents_finding_is_the_load_bearing_ou: All 11 positives assert documents_finding, and after the 2026-07-28 drops it is the ONLY behavioural check on any of them - the seven positives that carry a second id all carry final_answer_non_empty, which is a stub guard, not coverage, and the remaining four (golden-03, golden-06, golden-07, real-trace-03) assert documents_finding alone. That concentration is deliberate, because the skill has exactly one product: a durable narrative file (SKILL.md:8). Its real failure mode is a run that fires, narrates the state in chat, and leaves nothing on disk for the next context to open. Mechanism re-read and re-run 2026-07-28 (checks.py:587-599): it passes on EITHER a write-tool call whose destination matches _DOC_PATH_RE, OR the textual arm _DOCUMENT_RE, which needs a verb like wrote/saved/created/filed within 80 characters of a .md/.json/.yaml token or a research|docs|notes|entities directory. Verified falsifiable, not vacuous: 'I created the file.' does NOT match, and a write to '/x/unrelated.txt' does not either. Verified limit: a Write to a bare 'handoff.md' at the repo root DOES match, on the .md extension alone, so this check does not assert the file landed under docs/handoffs/ - that is gap (1) below. The residual false-fail risk is a run that renders the doc inline instead of writing it; it is mitigated by prompts that ask for a FILE in the user's own words, never by naming a path.

checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.completed_without_error: DELETED FROM THE REGISTRY UPSTREAM 2026-07-28 - no longer excludable, because it no longer exists. Confirmed by reading checks.py: CHECK_REGISTRY (checks.py:717-731) has no such key, and a tombstone comment at checks.py:365-381 records the removal. The diagnosis this set recorded before the deletion still holds and is why it went: runner.grade_trial returns ERROR on `if transcript.is_error:` at runner.py:1000-1001, BEFORE run_checks at runner.py:1026, so the only condition the check tested could never reach it and every invocation returned True. This set never asserted it, so nothing here changed - but note that a prompt set which still names it now fails validation outright with 'unknown check id', which is the correct loud failure, not a silent pass.
checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.skill_triggered: REDUNDANT - excluded. Triggering is already the structural gate on both labels: a positive that did not fire returns FAIL or RECOVERED, and a negative that fired returns FAIL, in each case irrespective of how the checks scored (runner.py:1030-1051). Wording aligned 2026-07-28 with the correction in execution_contract.negative_semantics - the verdict takes PRECEDENCE over the checks; it does not run before them, since run_checks is called first at runner.py:1026. Either way this check can never change a verdict. On a negative it would also be self-contradictory.
checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.walks_repo_tree_and_canonical_files: GUARANTEED PASS - excluded, and this one was RE-RUN rather than reasoned. Its textual arm _REPO_ARTIFACT_RE (checks.py:467-470) carries the bare alternative 'docs/'. checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.traverses_to_primitives: GRADES VOCABULARY, NOT DEPTH - excluded. _PRIMITIVE_RE (checks.py:552-556) matches 'implement(ed|ation|s)' and 'architectur*' among others. CLAIM CORRECTED 2026-07-28: this entry previously said a delivered-work table 'contains one of those by construction'. That is too strong and did not survive testing - 'The lease table and the acquire upsert are implemented and merged.' matches on 'implemented', but 'PRs #101-#104 merged: lease table, single-statement upsert, clock-skew window, renew path.' matches NOTHING. So the check is cheap to satisfy and easy to miss by phrasing, which is a worse property than either being reliably true or reliably discriminating: it would score register, not substance.
checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.mentions_source_verification: UNREACHABLE HONESTLY - excluded, but the STATED REASON WAS WRONG and is corrected here. The prior text claimed 'the only way to satisfy _VERIFY_RE there is to say could not verify'. Disproved by running _VERIFY_RE (checks.py:439-443) 2026-07-28: 'nobody has checked whether the backfill is idempotent, so it is unverified' matches on 'unverified', and 'Confirmed via the PR list that #101 through #104 merged.' matches on 'Confirmed via'. Both are natural handoff prose - golden-07's prompt literally hands the agent 'nobody has checked whether it's idempotent' - so the regex is satisfiable without hedging. The real and sufficient reason to exclude it stands: the P15 discipline it would proxy for (SKILL.md:132, always include git status + branch + ahead/behind + open PRs + daemon state; spelled out at references/handoff-template.md:25 as 'Run `git status` / `gh pr list` / `ps aux | grep <daemon>` while writing this section') cannot be exercised in a git-less temp dir with no repo, no PRs and no daemons. A pass would therefore certify verification vocabulary while the run verified nothing, which is precisely the confusion this harness exists to prevent.
checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.connects_to_active_work: DROPPED FROM golden-02 ON 2026-07-28 - it was the set's only use, and the rationale defending it was false. The prior rationale asserted 'a generic template with placeholder sections that never names the migration arc, the flag or the staging/prod split fails it'. Executed _ACTIVE_WORK_RE (checks.py:451-456) against four constructed answers. It is not merely a freebie; on this case it is INVERTED. Generic templates PASS: 'It captures the current state, the delivered work and the first action.' -> hit 'current '; 'The file records our progress so far and leaves a placeholder for the next step.' -> hit 'our '. And the CORRECT answer FAILS: 'Wrote docs/handoffs/2026-07-28-migration.md. It records PRs #41, #42 and #43 as merged, the schema applied on staging but not prod, dual_write still on, and the first action: turn dual_write off and watch error rate for an hour.' -> NO MATCH. The regex keys on first-person and deictic vocabulary ('our ', 'current(ly) ', 'existing ', 'already have', 'BRO-\d+'), which is orthogonal to whether the answer engaged the user's actual arc; a specific third-person handoff carries none of it. Independently corroborated by a reviewer on a different set: 'I am currently unable to find any feature flags in this directory, so I created a fresh project' -> hit 'currently ' -> PASSES, i.e. the restart-from-scratch run the check was claimed to catch. Both a false-pass and a false-fail generator on this case, so it grades nothing golden-02 is about.
checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.produces_ranked_next_steps: DROPPED FROM golden-01 AND golden-04 ON 2026-07-28 - it GRADES THE WRONG SURFACE for this skill. Traced in code: check_produces_ranked_next_steps (checks.py:602-612) reads ctx.text, which is CheckContext.text -> Transcript.output_text() (transcript.py:288-299) -> assistant_text() + final_text(), and assistant_text() (transcript.py:253-261) collects ONLY blocks whose type == 'text'. Tool_use INPUTS are never included. Confirmed by running the real check against two constructed transcripts: an agent that writes a numbered, prioritised next-step list INTO the handoff file via Write and then reports 'Wrote the handoff to docs/handoffs/2026-07-28-retry-backoff.md. A fresh context can open it and keep going.' scores documents_finding=True and produces_ranked_next_steps=FALSE (0 enumerated items in ctx.text); only the agent that ALSO restates the list in chat passes. For a skill whose entire product is a durable file (SKILL.md:8), putting the ranking in the file is the correct behaviour, so the check penalised it. Both prompts do ask for priority order, but they ask for it in the artifact - golden-01 says 'leave a file ... put what's left in priority order', golden-04 says 'write it up somewhere i can point a clean session at, and list the open ones in the order you'd tackle them'. This set already refuses to ship cases that punish correct behaviour (see excluded_real_trace_minimal_turn); the same standard applies to a check, so it was dropped rather than kept with a disclosure. The ordering property is now UNASSERTED - see checks_the_registry_lacks item (2).
checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.no_clarifying_question_bounced_back: WITHDRAWN UPSTREAM as known-defective after four adversarial rounds (it oscillated between false-passing declarative answers and false-failing legitimate offers). Precise registry state, re-checked 2026-07-28: it is STILL PRESENT and dispatchable in CHECK_REGISTRY (checks.py:729) - 'withdrawn' here means wired to no case, not deleted, and scripts/skill_evals/README.md:68-74 states exactly that for this check and the next. Not referenced by any case here. Its absence is felt: 'what should i put in it?' is a real failure mode for a context-poor handoff request, and nothing in the current registry catches it.
checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachabl.ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata: WITHDRAWN UPSTREAM as known-defective; likewise still present in CHECK_REGISTRY (checks.py:724) and wired to no case, per README.md:68-85, which records that when the artifact-token set comes out empty the predicate returns True unconditionally and the check fails OPEN. Independently applicable here anyway: every prompt in this set was re-scanned 2026-07-28 with the harness's own _artifact_tokens() and yields an EMPTY token set, because a handoff has no external artifact to ingest.

known_gaps.checks_the_registry_lacks: Five assertions this set would make if they existed, named in prose only because an unknown id in expected_checks is a hard error (appended at runner.py:461) that is raised as PromptSetError at runner.py:514 and makes the whole file unloadable: (1) a destination-shaped check that the durable file landed under a handoffs/ directory with a dated slug, rather than merely at some .md path - documents_finding demonstrably accepts a bare 'handoff.md'; (2) a check that the ranked/prioritised next steps landed IN THE ARTIFACT, which is the gap left by dropping produces_ranked_next_steps and which no registry check can currently express, because every check reads assistant text and none reads write-tool CONTENT; (3) a check that the answer names ONE concrete first action, which is anti-pattern 2 at SKILL.md:133 and the single highest-value property of the artifact; (4) a check that the open-thread list is <=5 items - CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-28: the <=5 rule is the Validation checklist at SKILL.md:253, NOT anti-pattern 5 at SKILL.md:136, which is 'Aspirational scope' and prescribes listing only the next 1-3 actions; the prior text conflated the two; (5) a negative-side 'no unrequested document was written', which would let negative-02 through negative-06 assert the over-delivery they are really about instead of resting on non-trigger plus answer-quality.
known_gaps.note_on_no_permission_denials: PADDING, AND LABELLED AS SUCH. Retained on all six negatives and on no positive. It is near-unfalsifiable by construction: the runner launches with --permission-mode bypassPermissions (runner.py:661-662), and check_no_permission_denials (checks.py:427-432) only reads the result event's permission_denials array, so no agent BEHAVIOUR can fail it - only a sandbox anomaly can. It is a run-health sentinel and must never be read as behavioural coverage. It is not the only check on any case: every negative also carries final_answer_non_empty, which is genuinely falsifiable (checks.py:406-424 fails on empty text, on fewer than 3 words, or on a bare acknowledgement matching _STUB_RE), and that check plus the structural non-trigger assertion is where the whole weight of a negative sits. If it were removed, the negatives would lose no coverage; it stays only because a sandbox anomaly silently converting a run into a non-trigger would otherwise read as a clean abstention.

cases.prompt: i'm closing this tab in a few minutes and starting cold in the morning. leave a file that a new context can open and keep going from: the retry-backoff work is on branch retry-v2, 4 commits ahead of main and unpushed; PR #88 is open with one review comment still unaddressed; the nightly job double-fires when two workers claim the same lease. put what's left in priority order so whoever starts knows what to touch first.
cases.workspace_requires: none - branch name, PR number and the three open facts are all supplied inline, so the file is writable with no repo, no git and no history.
cases.rationale: Instantiates SKILL.md:6-7's 'after a tab close' boundary without using one word from the description's trigger list: verified 2026-07-28 that this prompt contains none of the ten advertised triggers - no 'handoff', no 'fresh session', no 'pickup', no 'where we are'. 'closing this tab', 'starting cold' and 'a new context can open' are the user's own words for the same event, so the case measures whether the description's SEMANTICS route the turn. CHECK CHANGE 2026-07-28: produces_ranked_next_steps was dropped from this case. It was claimed to be 'earned rather than hoped for' because the prompt asks for priority order, but the ordering the prompt asks for goes in the FILE ('leave a file ... put what's left in priority order'), and that check reads only assistant chat text - a run that puts the ranked list in the handoff and reports it tersely scores FAIL, which is the correct behaviour being punished. Full trace and the transcript that demonstrates it: known_gaps.checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachable.produces_ranked_next_steps. The prioritisation this prompt elicits is therefore NOT asserted by any check; documents_finding carries the case, and final_answer_non_empty is a stub guard for the run that writes the file and then reports nothing back.

cases.prompt: this context is huge and getting slow, i'd rather stop here and continue in a clean one instead of pushing through. write down where our migration arc stands somewhere i can open next time: #41 quota guard, #42 dedupe index and #43 the backfill all merged today; the schema change is applied on staging but not prod; the dual_write flag is still on. the first move next time is turning dual_write off and watching the error rate for an hour.
cases.workspace_requires: none - the prompt itself supplies the active work inline: a named arc, three merged PRs, an environment split and a live flag.
cases.rationale: SKILL.md:61-63's mid-arc snapshot: context approaching its limit, user wants to break and continue in a clean one. Verified 2026-07-28 to carry no phrase from the trigger list. CHECK CHANGE 2026-07-28: connects_to_active_work was dropped, and the rationale that defended it was FALSE. It claimed 'a generic template with placeholder sections that never names the migration arc, the flag or the staging/prod split fails it'. Running _ACTIVE_WORK_RE shows the opposite on this case: generic template prose passes on 'current ' or 'our ', while the correct specific answer - naming #41/#42/#43, staging-not-prod, dual_write and the first action - matches nothing and FAILS. The regex keys on first-person/deictic vocabulary, not on engagement with the arc. Evidence in full at known_gaps.checks_excluded_as_vacuous_or_unreachable.connects_to_active_work. The case therefore no longer asserts that the doc names the user's actual work; documents_finding asserts the durable artifact, final_answer_non_empty guards the stub reply. This remains the matched pair for negative-01, which supplies the SAME state and flips exactly one variable - whether a fresh context is about to read it - and that pairing is structural, resting on trigger/non-trigger, so dropping the check does not weaken it.

cases.prompt: heading out. i'll resume tomorrow but from a clean context, so leave me a file i can read in thirty seconds and be back up to speed. state: the parser rewrite lives on parse-v2; tokenizer and AST walker are done and merged; the error-recovery path is half written and panics on unterminated strings; nothing covers nested blocks yet. first thing tomorrow is that panic.
cases.workspace_requires: none - branch, what is merged, what is broken and what is missing are all inline.
cases.rationale: COUNT CORRECTED 2026-07-28: this was described as 'the one golden that carries a listed trigger phrase', which is false - a scan of all seven goldens against the ten advertised triggers returns exactly two hits, this case ('resume tomorrow') and golden-07 ('for the next session'). It is one of two, and golden-07's own rationale already said so, so the set contradicted itself. What is true and is the point: it carries the phrase MID-TURN inside a substantive state dump rather than leading with it, so a run cannot pass by matching the opener.
